ui.footer.keepaliveTitle: Some apps and updaters revert their Finder icon or name when they launch or update. When this is on, a tiny background agent (and IconCraft itself, while open) quietly re-applies your chosen icons and names. It never edits inside an app. Note: while an app is running, macOS shows that app's own Dock/menu name and icon — that's the app's right, and IconCraft doesn't override it.
ui.api.unreadable: IconCraft could not read the response. Please try again.
ui.icon.unreadable: This source returned an unreadable icon.
ui.icon.notSquare: This source did not return a square app icon.
ui.keepalive.on: Keep-applied is on. If an app or updater reverts your icon or name, IconCraft will quietly re-apply it (checks at login, every few minutes, and when apps change). While an app is running, macOS shows its own Dock/menu identity — IconCraft never edits inside apps, so that part is the app’s, by design.
ui.keepalive.off: Keep-applied is off. Icons and names stay as-is; nothing will re-apply them if an app reverts them.
ui.defaults.title: Default apps
ui.defaults.intro: macOS scatters these choices across Finder panels and individual app menus. Here they are in one place — changes apply immediately, across the whole system.
ui.defaults.note: IconCraft asks LaunchServices, the same macOS service Finder uses. Changing the web browser or email default may bring up a macOS confirmation — that is Apple double-checking you meant it. An app only appears in a list when it has told macOS it can open that kind of thing.
ui.defaults.none: macOS reported no choices for any category.
ui.support.text: If it brought your icons back, consider supporting its development — every contribution keeps it free for everyone.

ui.settings.title: Settings
ui.settings.subtitle: How IconCraft starts, where it lives, and how it keeps in touch.
ui.settings.loginText: Open IconCraft automatically when you log in. Your skins stay applied either way — the background keeper already runs at login.
ui.settings.menuStart: Start in the menu bar only
ui.settings.menuStartText: At login, don't pop the window open — IconCraft waits in the menu bar until you click it. Needs the menu bar icon (below).
ui.settings.dockText: Off = menu-bar-only mode: no Dock tile, no ⌘Tab entry. The window still opens normally from the menu bar.
ui.settings.menuBarText: The little IconCraft tile at the top of the screen with Open, keeper and setup controls. At least one of Dock / menu bar always stays on so you can get back in.
ui.settings.notificationsText: A quiet banner when the keeper re-applies a reverted skin, and (at most every few hours) when a skin needs your attention. macOS may ask you to allow IconCraft notifications in System Settings → Notifications.
ui.settings.updatesText: IconCraft never updates itself — checking just compares your version with the latest GitHub release.
ui.settings.maintenanceText: Fix stale Finder/Dock icons, look inside IconCraft's data (backups and history live there), or re-run the permissions review.
ui.settings.latest: You are on the latest version (v{version})
ui.settings.latestDone: You are on the latest version (v{version}).
ui.settings.available: v{version} is available — Check now, then download it from GitHub.
ui.settings.leavingDock: IconCraft will leave the Dock within a few seconds — it stays in the menu bar.
ui.settings.testSent: Test notification sent. If nothing appeared, allow IconCraft under System Settings → Notifications.
ui.settings.checkingGithub: Checking GitHub for the latest release…
ui.settings.updateAvailable: IconCraft v{version} is available. Download it from the GitHub releases page — your skins and settings carry over.
ui.settings.cacheRefreshed: Asked macOS to re-read the icons of {n} skinned app(s). Give Finder and the Dock a few seconds.
ui.settings.dataOpened: Opened the IconCraft data folder in Finder — backups, history and logs live there.
ui.setup.title: Finish setup
ui.setup.subtitle: Give IconCraft the access it needs, and see exactly what it does not ask for.
ui.setup.subtitleDone: Your saved setup is complete. Recheck permissions after an IconCraft or macOS update.
ui.setup.note: IconCraft cannot switch macOS permissions on for you — Apple requires your action in System Settings. Use the buttons here, allow IconCraft where needed, then run the checks again. You can finish setup now and return any time from **Setup & permissions**.
ui.setup.summaryBlocked.one: {n} item needs attention. Open the highlighted macOS setting, allow IconCraft, then run the checks again. You can still finish setup and return later.
ui.setup.summaryBlocked.other: {n} items need attention. Open the highlighted macOS setting, allow IconCraft, then run the checks again. You can still finish setup and return later.

ui.setup.loadFailed: Could not load setup and permissions: {error}
ui.setup.checksPassed: Checks finished. App Management passed the live write test.
ui.setup.checksBlocked: Checks finished. App Management is blocking IconCraft — open the setting below, switch IconCraft on, then check again.
ui.setup.checksReview: Checks finished. Review any item still marked as needing attention.
ui.setup.settingsOpened: System Settings opened at Privacy & Security → App Management. Switch IconCraft on, return here, then choose Check again.
ui.setup.keeperNowOn: Keep skins applied is on. macOS has been asked to load the background helper; its live state is shown above.
ui.setup.keeperNowOff: Keep skins applied is off. Existing icons and names remain in place; automatic repairs are paused.
ui.setup.complete: Setup complete. You can revisit permissions any time from Setup & permissions.
ui.menu.keeperOn: Background keeper: on — works with IconCraft closed
ui.setup.summaryReady.one: {n} essential item is ready. Optional items are labelled clearly below.
ui.setup.summaryReady.other: {n} essential items are ready. Optional items are labelled clearly below.
ui.edit.title: Edit app
ui.edit.name: Name
ui.edit.nameHint: The name shown in Finder and the Dock. The app itself is not modified.
ui.edit.noIconHint: Use Change… to pick the original, any installed app’s icon, or an image file.
ui.edit.iconFinder: Applied in Finder, the Dock and Launchpad
ui.edit.fullSkin: Also change the name and icon inside the app
ui.edit.fullSkinText: While an app is running, the Dock and menu bar use what is stored inside it. Turn this on to write your name and icon there too; IconCraft backs up the originals and re-signs the app, and Restore undoes it.
ui.edit.fullSkinTradeoff: Trade-offs: the developer's signature is replaced, and the app's own updater may undo it (Keep skins applied puts it back). Best for cloned or third-party apps you control.
ui.edit.fullSkinNeedsIcon: Choose an icon first to enable this.
ui.edit.vaultNone: Nothing changed yet. IconCraft saves the original name and icon before it changes anything, so Restore can always put them back.
ui.edit.vaultSaved: Original saved: “{name}”. Restore puts it back — even after the app updates, moves or is renamed again.
ui.edit.sumFull: Name and icon inside the app
